The centre yields when resistance costs more than yielding: separatism takes land from the centre, which it will fight for; the protocol takes only the apathetic, and nobody will defend them by name (059l §8b, nonpolitical judo 40bh §4). Catalonia had a leader who could be jailed; the protocol's organisers are replaceable (40bh §2). All the cases are from democracies; for an autocracy the answer is 40bh §3: an autocrat cannot cancel a referendum on money for the family without losing legitimacy.

**Step zero without an organisation: a petition on a campaigning platform (26.10.2026).** A private referendum needs an institute, money and a measurement plan (048l). Before it there is a step that needs nothing: citizens' petition platforms — MyUplift in Ireland (my.uplift.ie: "petitions on this site are started and run by members of the public", the platform neither endorses nor runs the campaigns), and their analogues elsewhere. On 26.10.2026 the architect published there the petition "€2,000 or your vote: put the question to the people", addressed to "members of the Dáil and the Seanad" (Article 27): the text — the answer to the platform's question "why is it important" — opens with "because today your vote changes nothing, and everyone knows it", gives the rule in one paragraph, three gains (the vote stops being a ritual; the government gets a reason to raise the median; the price is 9 % of the surplus) and the request to a third of the Dáil (057g §6). What a petition gives and does not give: it is neither a referendum nor a measurement — the interested sign, and it will not show the share of takers. It gives three things: a number of signatories a deputy cannot fail to see; a list of people to whom the question with the price can be put for real (a private referendum by 048l among the signatories is already a sample, biased as it is); and a test of the wording on living people before money is paid for it. This is the first link of the move "forbidden, but possible" (006b §3c): petition → private referendum → an underdog with the number → Article 27. The outcome, the moderation and the growth of signatures are a measurement, kept daily, and will land here.

## What the protocol does not propose

The AI adviser in the architect's experiment added four things of its own. They are not in the repository, and they should not be done.

| The model's advice | Why not |
|---|---|
| Put money in an account and pay it to voters if the candidate wins | this is bribery of voters; under the protocol the budget pays by a rule adopted by referendum, and never the candidate |
| "Elect me — I will sign a decree" | elected bodies neither introduce nor alter the charter (048m, Article 14) |
| Route campaign money through a separate structure to get round the limits | a breach of campaign-finance law; the protocol has no need of it |
| A vote multiplier for those who refuse the payment | there is no such rule: one ballot — one vote (answer 10) |

========================================================================
PART 4. INDEX OF OBJECTIONS - EACH IN THE OPPONENT'S WORDS
========================================================================

## "This is vote-buying"

**What is true:** the outward likeness — money is paid for a decision about voting.
**Answer:** vote-buying is when a candidate or a party pays for a vote or for turnout in its own favour. Here the budget pays under law, equally to everyone who does not vote at this election, and asks nobody to vote for anyone; under the charter a candidate can never pay (048m, Art. 1 part 4). The payment buys not a vote but an honest count: today the non-voter sits at home unpaid and uncounted; under the rule he is counted and paid.
**In full:** [040as §1](../06-critique-arsenal/040as-walzer-sandel.md) (Walzer: the ban on selling the vote is violated today — bringing-in, benefits, party funding; a payment from the budget is a tax rebate that removes bribery; the protocol enforces the ban rather than breaking it), [1d](001d-exact-answers.md), [029](../06-critique-arsenal/029-hypocrisy.md), [045](../10-usa/045-us-legal-base.md).
**Unknown:** how the court of a particular country will classify it.

## "Paying people not to vote is voter suppression"

**What is true:** a word with a history, and the rival's ad writes itself.
**Answer:** voter suppression is obstacles that some put in the way of others: queues, purges, closed polling places. Here there are no obstacles: the right remains, the person makes the choice himself, anew at the next election, and nobody can make it for him. The candidate's lawful formula: "I support and will promote a referendum by every lawful means" — advocating a ballot measure is political speech, not payment for a vote.
**In full:** [048n, step 4](../08-implementation/048n-underdog-questions.md), [1d](001d-exact-answers.md).

## "A tax on the poor: the rich man stays at the polls, the poor man sells his vote for pennies"

**What is true:** money is worth more to those who have less of it; the filter by horizon falls on the poor more often, and we must say so before the opponent does.
**Answer:** the choice is the same for everyone, nobody loses a right, and the payment is a percentage of the median — for a poor person a noticeable sum, not pennies. Today the poor voter receives promises before an election; under the rule, a right to money he need not take. Selection is by stake, not by income: the poor man who has something to lose at this election stays; the rich man who no longer cares leaves.
**The architect's move (29 October 2026):** "You always speak of the rich man as a swindler who stole or took money from the poor. And yes, that was so for 2,000 years, but today wealth has partly remained with such people, while most of the rich are the middle class, and they earned it honestly with their minds and skills. I noticed this in you long ago: you take politicians and the rich by default for those who deceived the apathetic, seized power by fraud and then robbed the people. In our time that has long not been so in most countries. Yes, there are swindlers and helicopter rich, but their share is a few per cent, while the middle class and most of the rich are honest and noble people. And yes, on top of that it is easier for them to refuse D." The rich man for whom refusing D is easy is, in most countries today, not the one who took from the poor but the middle class that earned by mind and skill; he pays the taxes from which the payment comes, and his stake in governance is higher; that it is easier for him to stay is the design of the rule, not its vice ([040m §5d, the ninth rule](../06-critique-arsenal/040m-cold-reader-audit.md); [040b §5](../06-critique-arsenal/040b-hanson-futarchy.md)).
**In full:** [1d](001d-exact-answers.md), [013f §4](../03-theory/013f-formal-statement.md), [019b](../04-electoral-dynamics/019b-poor-voter-price.md), [1f §7](001f-core-electorate.md); the variant "the poor will take, the rich will stay — you amplify the bias" — [040aw §2](../06-critique-arsenal/040aw-gilens-page.md): the hall is counted in three movements, not two — the takers leave, the burned return, the rich remain a tenth.
**Unknown:** selection by income against selection by stake is measured only by a pilot — the main open question ([040m §4](../06-critique-arsenal/040m-cold-reader-audit.md)).

## "Only the radicals, the fanatics and the union activists will remain"

**What is true:** an activist with a stake — a contract, a wage, a job — will not take the payment; every model finds this, and it is so.
**Answer:** the protocol does not count on the activist. Two others leave by themselves: the one who comes without wishing to, because he was asked, and the one who no longer cares; and it brings back the burned — those who stopped coming because they could not outvote the machine. Today the moderate voter is not "at the polls" — he is at home, and his vote already does not count; the rule gives him a reason to return that he does not have now. "60 % of normal people will abandon the city for a trifle" is a number without a source.
**In full:** [1f §6–7](001f-core-electorate.md), [011b §11b.2c](../02-history/011b-learned-helplessness.md), [048n](../08-implementation/048n-underdog-questions.md), [040m §5i–5j](../06-critique-arsenal/040m-cold-reader-audit.md), [040bo §3](../06-critique-arsenal/040bo-montaigne.md).
**Unknown:** which group responds more strongly is a matter of measurement ([048n, "Measuring the question"](../08-implementation/048n-underdog-questions.md)).

## "A death spiral: the worse the city does, the more people take the payment, the worse for the budget"

**What is true:** in a crisis more people will take the payment — and that is the signal.
**Answer:** the sign is the opposite. The payment is a percentage of the median: when the city's income falls, the payment falls with it, automatically. And a rise in the number taking it is not a flight from the budget but a counter that shows the authorities the price of their work before the election, while it can still be corrected. The city does badly without the protocol too; the difference is that under it this is visible in a number, not in rumours. The payment is an unconditional obligation, a tax in reverse (048m, Art. 8 part 5); bankrupt cities exist without it, and the comparison must be with the present order, not with an ideal.
**In full:** [018 §34](../04-electoral-dynamics/018-three-epochs.md), [015b](../03-theory/015b-catharsis-spiral.md), [048m Arts. 2 and 8](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md).

## "Where is the money in the first year? That is hundreds of millions"

**What is true:** in the first cycle there are payments and no savings yet.
**Answer:** the size is a parameter: the percentage of the median and the share who take it. For a city of a million the table is in [1e](001e-by-role.md): at one percent of the median and half taking it — of the order of one percent of the city budget; "hundreds of millions" is a number to be calculated, not named. The money accumulates over the cycle or is raised by a targeted loan; the payment cannot be reduced or postponed (Art. 8 part 5). Where to find it in a particular city is a question of audit, not of the protocol: fund surpluses, no-bid contracts, hiring.
**In full:** [1e](001e-by-role.md), [1d, statement 9](001d-exact-answers.md), [048m, remarks of the legal reading](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md).
**Unknown:** in the US the loan of Article 8 is a legal question (bond counsel, public purpose); the first cycle is probably accumulation or a donor's guarantee.

## "The candidate promises people money if he is elected"

**What is true:** every second reader will read it so.
**Answer:** under the charter that is impossible, and the candidate does not promise it. He promises one thing: to seek a referendum. The money appears if the citizens vote for the rule, and the budget will pay — under any mayor, whoever the candidate. Whether he himself wins the rule does not promise and cannot.
**In full:** [048n, the ten steps](../08-implementation/048n-underdog-questions.md), [1d](001d-exact-answers.md).

## "A mayor cannot introduce this — the promise cannot be kept"

**What is true:** he cannot. Neither a mayor nor a president.
**Answer:** the protocol is introduced only by referendum, and that is written on the first page. The promise "I will introduce it" would be unkeepable; the promise "I will seek a referendum" is kept by collecting signatures, and its keeping is visible. If the signatures are not admitted, that is a separate fact about those who did not admit them.
**In full:** [048m Art. 15](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md), [048n, the signatures step](../08-implementation/048n-underdog-questions.md).

## "It will already apply at this election: his supporters get an amplified vote"

**What is true:** nothing — this confuses two elections.
**Answer:** at the election where the candidate proposes the rule, the rule does not yet exist: nobody takes a payment and nobody's vote is amplified; everyone votes as before. The rule takes effect after the referendum, at the following elections. Any calculation of the form "his base in the shrunken electorate becomes 20–23 %" describes an election under the protocol, of which there is none in this cycle.
**In full:** [048n, "Wanting the payment and voting for the candidate are different numbers"](../08-implementation/048n-underdog-questions.md), [1d, statement 15](001d-exact-answers.md).

## "People will register only for the cheque" (US)

**What is true:** in the US the register is voluntary registration, and with a payment it acquires a price.
**Answer:** for the referendum that is not a hole but a fuller list: those register who did not think it worth while before. False registration away from one's residence is a crime already; the protocol adds to it only an address check by the treasury before payment. The closing date of the roll an American charter must name explicitly.
**In full:** [048m, remarks](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md), [040m §5j](../06-critique-arsenal/040m-cold-reader-audit.md).

## "Whoever refuses the money gets a ×2 / ×3 vote multiplier"

**What is true:** the share of each ballot cast grows when some people step out.
**Answer:** there is no multiplier in the count for anyone: one ballot is one vote. The amplification is through share, equally for all who vote, whoever they vote for, and by how much is not known in advance. The slogan "an amplified vote" is right; "×2" as a counting rule is not.
**In full:** [1d, statements 11–12](001d-exact-answers.md).

## "The payment is $780 / 1/365 of the median / 1.5 % / 30,000 roubles"

**What is true:** such numbers exist on the site — in old worked examples and in role-play rounds.
**Answer:** the rule is a percentage of median income over the last twelve months, chosen by referendum; there is no fixed sum, and "1/365" exists nowhere. The table for a city of a million is in [1e](001e-by-role.md).
**In full:** [1d, statement 6](001d-exact-answers.md), [048m Art. 2](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md).

## "If 'against all' wins, the election is annulled and external administration follows"

**What is true:** nothing — a model's invention.
**Answer:** the protocol has no "against all", no annulment of elections and no external administration. The election is always held; the protocol adds one choice — vote or take the payment — and nothing more.
**The architect's move (30 October 2026), what follows in substance:** "It is important to separate two cases. If alternative candidates still exist, then with a large number of takers the alternative candidate gets a real chance of winning; and it is visible that not everyone is for the government, because many took the money. But if there is no alternative candidate, taking the money is equivalent to 'I vote against all'. And that is the line that every dictatorship or autocracy tries to remove from the ballot. They do it easily, because there is no difference between voting against all and not coming to vote, and the people agree to the deletion of that line." The protocol has no "against all" line, but choice B works as one — with two differences. First: it cannot be deleted, because it is not a line on the ballot but a payment with a receipt, and its disappearance would be noticed by everyone on his own card (Russia deleted the line by law in 2006, and nobody came out — there was nothing to delete but a line). Second: today "against all" and non-attendance are indistinguishable, which is why the line was given up without a fight; under the protocol they are distinguishable by art. 10 — the taker is counted separately from the one who did not come, and the share of takers is public ([057h §2.4](../09-other-countries/057h-serbia-2026.md), no-alternative).
**In full:** [048m](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md) entire; [048m art. 10](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md); [019 §60.2](../04-electoral-dynamics/019-bad-governance-cost.md) ("against all" as the cry of the burned).

## "Cash loses at the ballot box: Switzerland 23 %, Alaska, …"

**What is true:** the four cases are real — and all about something else.
**Answer:** a basic income is paid to everyone and always; here payment goes to the one who does not vote, once a cycle, and the size per cycle is 8–100 times smaller. The rule has two groups "for" that UBI lacks: those who will take it, and those who will stay and want to count. Alaska 1999 — the only referendum on the dividend — ended with 83 % for keeping it.
**In full:** [048n, question 7 and "Wanting the payment…"](../08-implementation/048n-underdog-questions.md).
**Unknown:** the rule has had no votes of its own.

## "Wanting the payment is not voting for the candidate"

**What is true:** entirely true.
**Answer:** the protocol says so itself: the candidate's road leads to a referendum, not to the chair. Whether the question moves votes to the candidate nobody knows; it is measured by one split in the campaign's poll, and until the table exists any figure is an invention.
**In full:** [048n, "Measuring the question: a poll is cheaper than an ad"](../08-implementation/048n-underdog-questions.md).

## "They will not come to the referendum: a free rider — the payment does not depend on turnout"

**What is true:** the difference from a job is real: vote or not, the rule will be adopted without you.
**Answer:** there is no quorum, a simple majority; people come to votes with a personal gain (Hungary 2026 — plus nine points of turnout once the bill was presented); and for a machine that brings voters the referendum is a fork: bring them and they vote "yes", do not bring them and lose.
**In full:** [048n, "The free rider at the referendum"](../08-implementation/048n-underdog-questions.md), [039](../06-critique-arsenal/039-levitsky-ziblatt.md).

## "The recipients will raise the percentage every cycle until the city is ruined"

**What is true:** the risk is real; in a very poor city a rise will pass.
**Answer:** the bill stands on the ballot beside the question; the payment falls with the median they themselves have lowered; the percentage can be changed no more than once a cycle; and a bankrupt city is a lesson to its neighbours, not the norm. A corporation that paid out too much in dividends is the same case.
**In full:** [018 §34](../04-electoral-dynamics/018-three-epochs.md), [048m Arts. 2 and 15](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md).

## "The protocol is against pensioners / wants to reduce the weight of old people's votes"

**What is true:** nothing — it weights no votes and knows no groups.
**Answer:** the filter is by the person: the horizon is a property of the person, not of age. A grandmother thinking of her grandson on the service register stays; a rich retired professor who no longer cares leaves. The chapter on the core electorate is about who decides now, not about who should not.
**The architect's move:** "the old are for stability and reliability, and money is more reliable than promises and forecasts — and they will remove themselves" — their own choice with money and the right to return, not exclusion; the community vote "out of duty" is a led vote, and with a secret choice community members will ask their elders how to get the payment ([040al §4](../06-critique-arsenal/040al-rove.md)).
**In full:** [1f §7](001f-core-electorate.md), [055c §6.9](../09-other-countries/055c-germany.md).

## "People want to participate but are not allowed: non-participation is the result of barriers"

**What is true:** barriers can be real, in an autocracy they are built on purpose, and the burned do not go while the count is foregone.
**Answer:** the architect: "there are people who do not want any of this, ever, until things are really bad and uncomfortable for them." The premise glues the burned (a minority, kept out) to the apathetic (a majority, unwilling). Removing barriers does not wake people: the 1993 motor-voter law did not raise turnout; Italy's 2025 referendums — about 30 %, the quorum not reached. Non-participation needs not access but a reasonable and safe exit — lawful, paid, secret and reversible; in an autocracy it takes from the regime what matters most — the apathetic — and producing them becomes unprofitable.
**In full:** [040bc](../06-critique-arsenal/040bc-q-people-want-to-participate.md), [040az](../06-critique-arsenal/040az-piven-cloward.md), [040av §1](../06-critique-arsenal/040av-schattschneider.md), [1f §6b](001f-core-electorate.md).
**What is unknown:** the shares of the apathetic and the burned among non-voters — a pilot measurement.

## "The protocol calls for rallies / overthrows dictators / with it there would have been no war"

**What is true:** "there would have been no war" is the architect's thesis, recorded as a thesis, with its boundary beside it.
**Answer:** the protocol is not an instrument of overthrow and calls for nothing; it is a rule under which deceit stops paying, because the payment leaves a trace in millions of bank records that cannot be forged at once. The chapters on Russia describe what the authorities can and cannot do, not what a citizen should do.
**In full:** [040n](../06-critique-arsenal/040n-guriev-treisman.md), [056f §13n–13q](../09-other-countries/056f-russia-september-2026.md), [055c §6.8](../09-other-countries/055c-germany.md).

## "Adopted nowhere, no data"

**What is true:** true. Not one pilot.
**Answer:** it is said on the first page. Everything that depends on the share who take the payment is an estimate; what does not depend on it — the arithmetic and the charter — is checked by reading. The first pilot is described with a budget and conditions.
**In full:** [048l](../08-implementation/048l-courtyard-pilot.md), [1d, statement 20](001d-exact-answers.md).

## "A supermajority is needed / a complicated procedure / a council decision"

**What is true:** nothing.
**Answer:** a referendum, simple majority, no quorum; neither a council nor a mayor introduces or repeals the rule. The "80 %" from the models is a simulation parameter, not a requirement.
**In full:** [048m Art. 15](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md), [1d](001d-exact-answers.md).

## "It will destroy civic duty: democracy put up for auction"

**What is true:** the word "duty" here is honest.
**Answer:** free mass non-voting everyone has already accepted as the norm: in Chicago two-thirds stay at home, and nobody calls that an auction. Explain what exactly in the compensation makes the same non-voting inadmissible. Seven models and hundreds of rounds gave no clean answer. The duty stays with the one who votes; the one who does not vote acquires a bill. And on "sanctity": very convenient when everyone guards for you, for free, what only you can use (029 §29.11).
**In full:** [001b](001b-essence.md), [037](../06-critique-arsenal/037-seventh-ai.md), [043 §76](../08-implementation/043-gemini-capitulation.md).

## "Someone's freedom not to vote for money infringes the rights of the rest"

**What is true:** every new freedom has a boundary — the rights of others (Mill).
**Answer:** checked against the charter one by one: the one who stays — one vote, a growing share; the taker — every other right and the vote in referendums on the charter; the one who chose neither — the vote and a late payment; nobody is excluded; no names are published; the freedom acts only on one's own vote and touches nobody else's. The only cost falls on the taxpayer, and he sets it himself by referendum like any budget line; the only new point of pressure — choice B — is protected by a criminal article and a secret channel. The protocol adds one freedom, takes none away and diminishes no right of anyone else.
**In full:** [039b §4b](../07-manifesto/039b-idealists-and-populist-cycle.md), [048m Arts. 1, 4, 5, 9, 11, 16](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md).

## "One who took the money loses rights" / "the choice can be reversed"

**What is true:** nothing.
**Answer:** he keeps every other right and votes in referendums on the rule itself; the choice is final within one election and made anew at the next. Otherwise — collusion and double counting.
**In full:** [048m Arts. 4 and 14](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md), [1d, statements 2, 5](001d-exact-answers.md).

## "A trust / a donor pays / there is a bonus for saving"

**What is true:** nothing — old editions.
**Answer:** only the budget pays; a separate line or a fund is a country setting. There is no bonus, the payment is one. A donor can fund a pilot, not the payment.
**In full:** [048m Art. 1 part 4, Art. 8](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md), [048l](../08-implementation/048l-courtyard-pilot.md).

## "This is populism: the people against the elite"

**What is true:** in four places the repository says "steals", "bribery" — the populist's register.
**Answer:** by Mudde's three markers the protocol is not populism: the people are neither homogeneous nor pure (four states, and the apathetic is the government's condition), the elite is not an enemy (the government is a predictable response to the composition), "we" is not permanent (the composition is re-elected every cycle, the taker keeps his rights and his vote on the rule). "Steals" is an economic term: a resource used for free without its owner's consent. The one-sentence test: the populist jails, the protocol presents a bill.
**In full:** [040ab item 1](../06-critique-arsenal/040ab-mudde.md), [1d, misreadings](001d-exact-answers.md), [029 §29.11](../06-critique-arsenal/029-hypocrisy.md).
**What is unknown:** a quotation is shorter than a mechanism; the defence works for a reader who reaches 1d.

## "The government will repeal the protocol as soon as it gets in its way"

**What is true:** the lock is weak — repeal by simple majority at a referendum (048m Arts. 14–15).
**Answer:** what protects is not the lock but self-enforcement: breaking the rule strikes "the takers" (money) and "those who stay" (share of the vote) at once, the line is bright (a number), the coordinator is ready (the opposition), the army is made of takers. It pays the government more to keep the rule than to break it (Przeworski: "the only game in town"). The closest analogy is the repeal of a universal subsidy (bread, fuel, the Alaska dividend), not the repeal of elections. Inflation does not eat a percentage of the median.
**In an autocracy — the architect's move:** "the autocrat cannot cancel the referendum: he would lose legitimacy himself, he pretends to be lawfully in power." A rule adopted by referendum is a piece of the legality the autocrat imitates; cancelling it by decree destroys the imitation and takes the payment away from millions of families by name ([040bh §3](../06-critique-arsenal/040bh-q-change-from-above.md)).
**In full:** [040v §6](../06-critique-arsenal/040v-przeworski.md), [040ag item 5](../06-critique-arsenal/040ag-tilly.md), [1c](001c-board-without-good-moves.md).
**What is unknown:** at the healthy pole "those who stay" may vote for a lower percentage (tax against share), but that is calibration, not erosion: the percentage settles where about half take the payment ([040v](../06-critique-arsenal/040v-przeworski.md)), which is the charter's own benchmark — the payment desirable for 40–50 % of the population (048m art. 3 part 3); where exactly it stops is a measurement. The referendum on the rule is not protected by the counter, because it has no choice B — a candidate for the charter decisions (048k §3).

## "A payment from taxes is the producers' money handed to parasites" (the Objectivist)

**What is true:** B is paid from the budget, that is, from the producers' taxes.
**Answer:** the apathetic's vote is already bought today — with benefits, indexations and promises — out of the same pocket, without a ceiling or a receipt. The protocol puts a price, a ceiling and a receipt on that purchase (D = p × M, from the charter), and the producer receives a weight of ×2 and above without leaving for the gulch. Compare not with a world without taxes but with a world where the apathetic is bought dearer and in the dark.
**Where in detail:** [040aj §7](../06-critique-arsenal/040aj-dalton.md), [040ab](../06-critique-arsenal/040ab-mudde.md), [040p](../06-critique-arsenal/040p-how-to-refute.md).
**What is unknown:** for one who rejects taxation as such, the comparison with the current system is not an argument; the dispute with him is not about the protocol.

## "The protocol suppresses the votes of the poor and of minorities: they are paid not to come"

**What is true:** the payment will more often be taken by those who need money now, and among them there are more of the poor.
**Answer:** nobody loses the vote — both rights, to vote and to take the payment, are kept forever and chosen anew at every election (048m art. 16, art. 5). Suppression is when a vote is taken away or devalued; the protocol adds a right, it does not remove one. The one suppressed today is the one whose vote is bought for a bus ride and a package of benefits and whose opinion nobody asks (1f §5, 030b). To decide for the poor that they may not take their own money is to take a right away from them.
**Where in detail:** [059l §8 row 11, §8b](../10-usa/059l-five-thousand-rehearsal.md), [040ab](../06-critique-arsenal/040ab-mudde.md), [1f §5](001f-core-electorate.md), [048m arts. 5, 16](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md); the variant "those who stay are a chorus with an upper-class accent" — [040av §4](../06-critique-arsenal/040av-schattschneider.md): without the protocol the upper class buys the chorus, after the protocol the chorus sings for its own money about its own problems.
**What is unknown:** the share of the poor among the takers — a pilot measurement; if it proves overwhelming, the dispute will be about the size of p, not about the right.

## "The numbers on the site are made up"

**What is true:** for the role-play chapters — true: the models' replies contain their own estimates.
**Answer:** such chapters are marked; the numbers in them are not the author's estimates. The rule and the arithmetic live in [1d](001d-exact-answers.md), [048m](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md) and [1e](001e-by-role.md); everything else is to be read as analysis, not as a source.
**In full:** [040m §5d](../06-critique-arsenal/040m-cold-reader-audit.md), the rules for a number.

## "Those who left must be included: those who stayed are more apathetic and dumber"

**What is true:** today diaspora votes are a counterweight to a full hall with the apathetic and bought votes (Moldova: about 78 % of the diaspora for PAS).
**Answer:** the architect: "who governs the country and knows it?" — the one who lives in it and pays. And: "activists want to include those who left out of resentment that those who stayed are dumber and more apathetic — but the protocol solves this before the election." The apathetic leave with the payment, a bought vote costs more than the bribe, the hall cleans itself from inside — no counterweight is needed. The payment follows tax residence; a non-resident's vote stays as today; one who returned and became a resident gets the full right. "Those who stayed are dumber" is selection from outside, as with franchise qualifications; the protocol evaluates no one and adds no one.
**In detail:** [048k §3, addition to decision 9](../08-implementation/048k-charter-inventory.md), [048m art. 4](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md), [019 §60.7](../04-electoral-dynamics/019-bad-governance-cost.md), [053](../09-other-countries/053-moldova.md).
**Unknown:** how many who left will return for a weighted vote — a measurement after the first cycle.

## "If it worked, it would have been introduced long ago; or someone invented it earlier and the government bought him"

**What is true:** over two thousand years of franchise qualifications nobody assembled the idea, though all the parts were in plain view.
**Answer:** checked 26.10.2026 — there is no predecessor with the three features together (a rule pays, for leaving, with weight for those who stay); payment for not voting lived for two thousand years only in the category "bribery" (18 U.S.C. § 597). Three locks, not a conspiracy: turnout was counted as health; buying non-attendance paid off only for a candidate; the parts lay in different disciplines. There is no proven case in history of the author of an electoral idea being bought, and there is nobody to buy: the protocol is a text. The architect's move — Gesell's money: known for a century, worked in Wörgl, and not introduced because the only introducer is the issuer, to whom it is unprofitable. The protocol has no single introducer: referendum and initiative pass those to whom it is unprofitable, and there is no loser by name.
**In detail:** [006b §3c](../02-history/006b-predecessors-and-gaps.md), [019 §61.6](../04-electoral-dynamics/019-bad-governance-cost.md), [048n](../08-implementation/048n-underdog-questions.md), [023f](../05-empirical-base/023f-money-at-elections.md).
**Unknown:** pamphlets and non-English sources not reviewed; a negative is not proved. Priority — the commit history since April 2026.

## "Serbia proved an autocrat can be removed without the protocol"

**What is true:** on 25 October 2026 a party that had ruled for fourteen years was replaced by an ordinary election on a 69 % turnout.
**Answer:** it took three conditions at once — an accident with sixteen dead that woke the apathetic; Europe's external oversight; two years of the street that made the awakened organised. Remove any one — 46 days, €600 m of payments and 129 television appearances work, as in 2023. None is created at the citizens' will, and none remains after the victory: the new government has no counter, the million register entries remain, the next early election again favours whoever calls it. The Serbs assembled nine mechanisms of the protocol by hand and paid for each; the protocol makes them a rule every cycle.
**In detail:** [057h](../09-other-countries/057h-serbia-2026.md), [013g](../03-theory/013g-decay-of-democracy.md), [40bh](../06-critique-arsenal/040bh-q-change-from-above.md).
**Unknown:** the 057h §5 forecast is checked by 2028–2030; if the street holds the result without a rule, that will have to be recorded.

## "The stayers are no better than the takers — merely more stubborn and more vain"

**What is true:** the stayers are neither wiser nor more virtuous; the protocol does not claim they are.
**Answer:** everyone in the hall compared two numbers — D and the worth of the vote to himself — and the vote came out higher; the taker counted too and chose the money; the only one who did not count is the one who was brought, and he is no longer in the hall. A hall of those who counted against a hall of those who did not. Stubbornness and self-assurance in a voter are another name for readiness to act on one's conviction and calculation; that is exactly what everyone who wrote about the republic demanded of the citizen, without an instrument to separate it. The fork: either the stayers really are more stubborn — and the hall consists of those every thinker wanted; or not — and the hall is no worse than today's, while the money went back to the people.
**In full:** [040bo §3](../06-critique-arsenal/040bo-montaigne.md), [040b §5](../06-critique-arsenal/040b-hanson-futarchy.md), [040bn](../06-critique-arsenal/040bn-hayek.md) (thesis 10).
**Unknown:** the share of the "showy" among the stayers — a measurement of [048l §4](../08-implementation/048l-courtyard-pilot.md).

========================================================================
PART 5. GLOSSARY - TERMS ARE STATES AND ECONOMIC TERMS, NOT JUDGEMENTS
========================================================================

| Term | Meaning | What it is not | In full |
|---|---|---|---|
| **the protocol**, AB-EXIT | the rule: before each election every voter chooses A — vote, or B — take the payment and sit this election out; introduced and repealed only by referendum | not a party, a candidate or a programme; it takes no power | [1b](001b-essence.md), [048m](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md) |
| **choice A / choice B** | vote / take the payment; B is final within one election, at the next the choice is made anew | not a status or category of citizen; rights do not depend on the choice | [048m Arts. 5, 16](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md) |
| **the payment** | a percentage of the jurisdiction's median income, set by referendum; only the budget pays | not vote-buying: vote-buying is when a candidate or party pays for a vote or for turnout; not a fixed sum | [1d, statement 6](001d-exact-answers.md), [1g](001g-objections-index.md) |
| **share of the vote**, amplification, "×3" | arithmetic: if two-thirds took the payment, each ballot cast is three times as large a share; equally for all who vote | not a multiplier or coefficient: one ballot is one vote | [1d, statements 11–12](001d-exact-answers.md) |
| **the counter** | public numbers: how many voted, how many took, how many did neither | not a rating or a poll — a fact from the election's results | [048m Art. 10](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md) |
| **the precinct balance** | reconciliation: the precinct's voters = those who voted + those who took + those who abstained; double spending is on the commission | not control over who chose what: names are not published | [048m Art. 5 part 3, Arts. 9–10](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md) |
| **the thermostat** | feedback: the more took, the higher the share of each remaining vote and the more it is worth returning — and they return; exit itself raises the price of entry | not a manual setting: both arms move at once, there is no lever | [1b](001b-essence.md), [040ae item 4](../06-critique-arsenal/040ae-sartori.md) |
| **state** (not type) | a voter's position at a given election — "apathetic", "burned" and so on; changes from election to election | not character, class or psychotype | [1f](001f-core-electorate.md) |
| **"apathetic"** | a voter with a short horizon for whom elections change nothing, and who votes only if brought | not "lazy" or "stupid": his estimate "my vote changes nothing" is accurate today | [1f §2, §5](001f-core-electorate.md), [040ae item 2](../06-critique-arsenal/040ae-sartori.md) |
| **"the meek"** | a voter who votes "so that it does not get worse", under fear of losing the little he has | not a coward: fear under dependence is rational | [1f §2](001f-core-electorate.md) |
| **"the centre": by motion and by position** | in polls "the centre" is those whose vote cannot be predicted by party; it mixes movers without a position ("the apathetic"-waverers, "the meek") and the standing with a position (the cross-pressured, "the burned") | triangulation takes the former and calls it the median voter; the protocol separates them: the movers take B, the standing get weight | [040ao §1](../06-critique-arsenal/040ao-morris.md) |
| **"the core"** | the composition that decides the outcome today: the budget-dependent, mostly older, who are brought. Not to be confused with **the elite** — the top that passed the selection and the rich attached to it: they live off the budget as beneficiaries, the core as recipients of crumbs; today they vote alike, under the protocol apart — the dependent take B, the elite is left at the polls alone and is visible at its true size for the first time (055e §6) | not "the enemy", not "fanatics", not "bad people" — a predictable response to dependence; and not the elite: the core is those at whose expense the elite lives | [1f §2, §2b, §2c](001f-core-electorate.md) |
| **"the brought-in"** | those delivered to the election — by fear, by the employer, by a promise, by bus | not "bought": they receive no payment, that is the point | [1f §5](001f-core-electorate.md), [040ac item 1](../06-critique-arsenal/040ac-lipset.md) |
| **"the layer"** | the thin wavering stratum that decides the outcome when two cores cancel each other; decides last, by image | not "the centre" or "the moderates" | [040v item 1](../06-critique-arsenal/040v-przeworski.md) |
| **"the burned"** | those who voted, saw the core could not be outvoted, and stopped going; they produce most of the product and the ideas; absent from the literature — nearest: Hirschman's exit, Dalton's "apartisans", the "exhausted majority" | not "disappointed idealists" or "the best": a description of a path, not of quality; and not the layer — they judge by substance, not by the speaker's face | [1f §6, §6b](001f-core-electorate.md), [040aj](../06-critique-arsenal/040aj-dalton.md) |
| **"the unburned"** | a young voter with a long horizon whose first election came already under the protocol: he never set out on the path through the core and took no burn; full of strength, wants to improve the world | not "burned" and not "returned" — a new state absent from 1f, because 1f describes the world before the protocol; within a generation "the burned" end as a group — they stop being produced | [040ai §4](../06-critique-arsenal/040ai-how-communism-arises.md) |
| **"those who stay"** | all who chose A at this election — whatever they were before | not "the real people", not "the elite": the composition of one election, different at the next | [040ab item 2](../06-critique-arsenal/040ab-mudde.md) |
| **"the takers"** | all who chose B at this election | not "sold out", not "excluded": the same rights, the vote in the referendum on the rule remains | [048m Art. 5 part 5, Art. 16](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md) |
| **"long / short horizon"** | how far ahead a voter counts consequences: beyond the cycle, or until tomorrow; depends on position (stake, dependence), not on intelligence | not "clever / stupid", not "young / old" | [1f §7](001f-core-electorate.md), [036e §10](../06-critique-arsenal/036e-nobel-fifth-circle.md) |
| **"thinking"**, "the thinking middle class" | one to whom the vote is worth more than the payment, because he has a stake beyond the cycle | not praise and not IQ: a synonym of "long horizon" in the context of choice A | [040v item 1](../06-critique-arsenal/040v-przeworski.md), [040af](../06-critique-arsenal/040af-muller.md) |
| **"remembering"** | a voter who at the second election will check what the representative said and did; memory is a consequence of stake | not a moral quality | [040x item 5](../06-critique-arsenal/040x-manin.md) |
| **"the government"** | the sitting elected and the apparatus; a predictable response to the composition of deciders | not "the enemy": the protocol names no enemies, it changes the composition and the government changes after it | [1f §2b](001f-core-electorate.md), the head of `llms-full` |
| **"the elite"** | those who nominate and are nominated | not "corrupt": Mudde's three-marker test — zero of three | [040ab item 1](../06-critique-arsenal/040ab-mudde.md) |
| **"steals"**, "appropriates" | an economic term: uses the citizen's resource (his vote, his turnout) for free and without his consent | not a moral verdict and not an accusation of crime; the protocol's answer is a price, not a punishment | [029 §29.11](../06-critique-arsenal/029-hypocrisy.md), [040ab item 1](../06-critique-arsenal/040ab-mudde.md) |
| **"bribery"** (of state party funding) | legally: payment from the budget for the vote, permitted by a law written by the recipients | not about the payment to the voter under the protocol — that is by a rule adopted by referendum | [040y item 3](../06-critique-arsenal/040y-mair.md) |
| **"populist"** | a politician whose support rests on the brought-in and the layer and whose promises address the short horizon | not a term of abuse: a description of the one from whom the protocol takes the free voter | [040ab item 5](../06-critique-arsenal/040ab-mudde.md), [039b](../07-manifesto/039b-idealists-and-populist-cycle.md) |
| **"underdog"** | a candidate not from the government who puts the protocol to a referendum because he has nothing to lose from a change of composition | not "a hero" and not "the opposition" in general | [048n](../08-implementation/048n-underdog-questions.md) |
| **"sick" jurisdictions** | cities and countries with low turnout, debt and no alternation, where the protocol is tested first | not an insult: "the sick first" is an order of testing, not a diagnosis of people | [040m §5d](../06-critique-arsenal/040m-cold-reader-audit.md), [048l](../08-implementation/048l-courtyard-pilot.md) |
| **"punishment or price"** | the populism test: the populist jails, the protocol presents a bill | — | [040ab item 1](../06-critique-arsenal/040ab-mudde.md) |
| **"the bounty trap"** | the error of comparing the protocol with an ideal instead of with the present system | — | [040m](../06-critique-arsenal/040m-cold-reader-audit.md) |
| **"passionarity"** | Gumilev's term, used in the repository operationally: the state of a voter at a given election in which the vote is worth more to him than D (p × M); measured by the share of stayers at a given p; coarse at the income edges, accurate on the middle class | not a heritable trait and not a theory of ethnogenesis; not "a radical" or "a sage"; in English — intensity of preference (Dahl) or revealed preference | [040bp](../06-critique-arsenal/040bp-gumilev.md) |

========================================================================
PART 6. REGISTER OF CONSEQUENCES - WHAT FOLLOWS FROM THE RULE WITHOUT BEING PROMISED
========================================================================

| Consequence | Mechanism | Planned? | In full | What is unknown |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **the roll becomes accurate and complete** — from a battlefield to a queue at the entrance | the payment goes to everyone on the roll; the unregistered enters himself, the purged goes to court himself; the government pays for dead souls and for the first time wants them gone; accuracy stops being partisan — both sides want one list from different ends | **no** — found 12 Oct 2026 in the SAVE examination | [059h](../10-usa/059h-voter-roll.md), [059g item 2](../10-usa/059g-midterms-2026-missouri-scenario.md) | the share of wrongful entries before and after |
| **the unprovability of the absence of fraud disappears** — for developed countries more important than fraud itself | in Russia the reservoir of the silent is used for stuffing; in the US and Spain hardly at all, but it exists (1.8M deceased, 2.5M silent on CERA), and while it exists the accusation "we were robbed" is irrefutable (2020, 2023, 2026), and half the country does not accept the result; the protocol gives every record an owner and every vote a second trace in money — consent to the outcome rests on arithmetic, not on faith in the commission | found 12 Oct 2026 (the architect's question: "do developed countries need accuracy") | [059h](../10-usa/059h-voter-roll.md), [057f](../09-other-countries/057f-spain-2026-cera.md), [040v §6, item 3](../06-critique-arsenal/040v-przeworski.md) | the share accepting the result before and after |
| **campaign technology loses three-quarters of its material** — without a single ban | the trade's ten tricks are designed for those who decide without thinking; the protocol pays the target to leave, and the tricks become not illegal but pointless: bringing in and stuffing −90–95 %, drying up turnout inverts, spoilers −40 %, average about −75 % 🟡; a hundred years of bans (bribery, limits, cordons) bred evasion because the target stayed in the hall | found 12–13 Oct 2026 (the architect: "for technologies that spoiled and distorted election results, a very good result") | [030b](../06-critique-arsenal/030b-ten-tricks.md) | which tricks the campaigns try first at the pilot |
| **the government's base splits by income: the elite stays, the dependent take** | the elite and the dependent vote alike today, the one living at the other's expense; the layer between them is narrow — the government cannot pay everyone well; the protocol cuts exactly along the gap: the dependent take B, the elite is visible at its true size for the first time — a few per cent | found 13 Oct 2026 (the architect's move) | [055e §6](../09-other-countries/055e-france-2027-forecast.md), [1h "the core"](001h-glossary.md) | the share of takers among low-paid budget employees against the upper ranks |
| **the second-term trap: an incumbent introduces the protocol as a last chance** | the first term was won on bringing-in, by its end bringing-in has stopped working and the run-off against a populist is a coin toss; the protocol changes the composition of deciders in favour of a long-horizon candidate; the instrument is a presidential referendum; a third route — from above; a win on any outcome | **no** — the architect, 13 Oct 2026: "I missed this second-term trap too" | [055e §4](../09-other-countries/055e-france-2027-forecast.md) | who is first: the underdog, the donor or the incumbent |
| **D is the numeraire of politics: programmes become commensurable** | both parties translate the promise into one currency ("is it worth more than D to you"), and they can be compared with each other by the same ruler; the waverer gets a scale instead of two images; a promise without a price is not made | **no** — the architect, 13 Oct 2026: "the numeraire is unplanned" | [040v item 1](../06-critique-arsenal/040v-przeworski.md), [013 §13.2](../03-theory/013-game-theory.md) | works for what money can value (housing, tax), less for war and rights |
| **the political decision moves from the party into each person's head** | "is the vote worth more than D to me, or not?" — each seeks the balance for himself, not in a class, party, nation or "the core"; groups are not banned — the decision no longer passes through them; class becomes impossible as a unit of decision | found 13 Oct 2026 (the architect's move) | [040ai §4](../06-critique-arsenal/040ai-how-communism-arises.md), [040r](../06-critique-arsenal/040r-arendt.md), [040ab](../06-critique-arsenal/040ab-mudde.md) | whether A/B choices diverge within the same groups |
| **campaigning changes genre: a party persuades its own not to take** | D is the reservation price of political attention; a party must prove to its own voter that the programme is worth more than D to him; "I am for you, but I will take" is a graded signal, a measurement of programme quality in money; the moral argument "do not take" is removed by the charter | found 13 Oct 2026 (the architect's move) | [040v item 1](../06-critique-arsenal/040v-przeworski.md) | the share of each party's own lost to the payment |

| poverty is a vote-price policy (hypothesis) | a regime on bought turnout rations prosperity: a vote is cheap only for the poor, a ration irreplaceable only for the destitute; oil rent goes into distribution through the regime's hands, not into incomes; the protocol makes the vote dear with one number — incompatible with such a regime by arithmetic | found 16 Oct 2026; the architect's hypothesis, not planned | [057d §3b](../09-other-countries/057d-venezuela.md), [057c §6b](../09-other-countries/057c-iran.md), [039 §88.9](../07-manifesto/039-opponents.md) | the share of rent going to distribution versus incomes, by country — uncounted; not the only cause of poverty |
| the government's interest and the growth of prosperity point the same way for the first time | a government on bought turnout keeps the voter cheap — poor and dependent (Acemoglu–Robinson 2006, Magaloni 2006, Robinson–Verdier 2013); the protocol makes its electorate those who cannot be bought, and the government loses its benefit in keeping people poor | found 16 Oct 2026; a property of the construction, not a consequence (the architect: "the cornerstone of all non-democratic regimes") | [013g §3b](../03-theory/013g-decay-of-democracy.md), [057d §3b](../09-other-countries/057d-venezuela.md) | — |
| the referendum on the rule is organised without the political class | the platform — open code (048m art. 15.4); the money — the takers' own contributions (040ap §4); the people — the burned, reached in one or two touches (040aq §4); the media — the topic runs without a machine (059l §2–3); the channel — the initiative, tested on Medicaid (040aw §3); the protocol is nobody's (059l §4). | the protocol's challenge pays for its own spread | the relay: the stake note moves between players at zero sum, the taker must play on, the one who chooses the vote pays and may close the chain or carry it on himself; a participant earns by closing the chain and by views; no organiser or centre is needed; every clip is a recorded pair "took or stayed" with a face, i.e. the 048l measurement without a budget | found 16–19 Oct 2026; the architect's move ("anyone watching can be invited to try to earn"), not planned | [048o](../08-implementation/048o-relay-challenge.md), [052 §90.15](../10-usa/052-676-challenge.md) | the share choosing the vote, the chain length and the response to "try it yourself" are unmeasured |
| the vote "against" gets an addressee with a name — a third candidate of the centre; fear mobilisation gets a price, the pendulum loses its axis | with a full hall a third candidate is a wasted vote (the Gallup gap: 62 % "want" / 15 % "will vote"); after the apathetic leave, the hall is those to whom the vote is worth more than the payment, and a non-party centre candidate is first by the median (022 §67.5, 059g); coming "against them" is free today, with the payment it costs $800 of refusal — the commodity of both campaigns (negative partisanship, the "pied piper," fundraising on the enemy) gets cheaper; both parties converge on the median of those who stay by Downs | found 19 Oct 2026; the architect's move ("after the apathetic leave, a third candidate gets a real chance, and that is the non-party centre"), not planned | [059n §5–6](../10-usa/059n-vote-against.md), [022](../04-electoral-dynamics/022-consensus-theme.md), [059g](../10-usa/059g-midterms-2026-missouri-scenario.md) | the direction of the shift by party and the share of the "against" leaving with money — a pilot question; Pew 44/19 (2026) is the only thermometer before the referendum |
| the protocol breaks any collective deal over votes | a bloc vote rests on a member coming and voting as told, with absence visible; under the protocol the choice is secret, the money goes to a personal card, nobody's permission is needed; the choice can be found out only by forcing people to vote, but by then it is irreversible and morally understandable (the architect) — the leader cannot deliver the bloc, only punish after the fact; union, community, ethnic and corporate blocs stop being a commodity | found 25 Oct 2026; the architect's generalisation ("it breaks any deals of a community, a union or any other; taking the money is lawful and simple, you need nobody's permission"), not planned | [015c §7b](../03-theory/015c-sign-change.md), [040al §4](../06-critique-arsenal/040al-rove.md) | a group with a standing grievance will stay to vote on its own (015c §7a) — that is not a deal but a common interest |
| the citizen's share for the first time in history cannot be recalled, and nothing is given up for it | every known share was grace or payment: Athens — for attendance, Rome — for loyalty, franchise qualifications — with the vote of the poor; Alaska's dividend cut by the governor's veto (2016, court 2017), Iran's 2010 payment eaten by inflation; under the protocol the amount is tied to the median (D = p × M), changeable only by referendum (art. 14), everyone takes it himself and secretly; the one who takes gets money, the one who stays gets double weight, nobody loses; in a rentier country this is the share of the rent | found 25 Oct 2026; the architect's move ("AB-EXIT is the first in history, and it is beautiful"), not planned | [057d §3b](../09-other-countries/057d-venezuela.md), [057c §6b](../09-other-countries/057c-iran.md), [019 §60.7](../04-electoral-dynamics/019-bad-governance-cost.md) | the size of p in a rentier country with a low median and a large rent is a decision of the country statute (057d §4) |
| a referendum on the rule passes even where the law says "no", if the question is clear and the majority clear | Quebec 1995 (court 1998, Clarity Act 2000): a clear majority on a clear question obliges the centre to negotiate; Scotland 2014: consent came from a repeated demand; Catalonia 2017: past the state machine — the opponent handed the argument of legality, the boycott devalued the result; the protocol's question is clearer than any (one rule, one number), it costs the centre nothing it would fight for, one who did not come is a recorded entry | found 26 Oct 2026; analysis of Katz's episode on Alberta, not planned | [048n](../08-implementation/048n-underdog-questions.md), [40bh](../06-critique-arsenal/040bh-q-change-from-above.md) | all cases are democracies; for an autocracy — 40bh §3 |
| a dispute over distribution is settled by price, not discord: there is no loser by name | in Machiavelli (I.37) quarrels over property ruined the republic because the agrarian law had someone robbed; the payment does not take but gives on top, to everyone equally, from a budget that already buys the apathetic vote; the sides do not fight but bargain — the share of takers as a quotation, D against promises every cycle, the sum visible to all | found 26 Oct 2026; the architect's move ("closer to economics and the equilibrium free price of a good, which balances everyone and does not let the seller war with the buyer"), not planned | [40bj §3](../06-critique-arsenal/040bj-machiavelli.md), [013 §13.10](../03-theory/013-game-theory.md), [019d](../04-electoral-dynamics/019d-market-price-of-vote.md) | the balance of the price — what share takes at what p — a pilot measurement |
| where there is no citizens' initiative the protocol is still introduced: "forbidden, but possible" | a private referendum (route B) gives a number the parliament does not have; a clear majority on a clear question obliges it to reckon (Quebec 1998); the underdog goes to the election with the number, no kamikaze against him; Gesell's money after its pilot had only the issuer, the protocol has someone to whom it is profitable; Ireland: Article 27 passes the opposition round the government, and 1928 shows the door is removed when touched — so the organisers are replaceable and the number cannot be repealed | found 26 Oct 2026; the architect's move ("if an independent referendum is held, and the Dáil sees the support, and an underdog is found — then forbidden, but possible"), not planned | [006b §3c](../02-history/006b-predecessors-and-gaps.md), [048l §2](../08-implementation/048l-courtyard-pilot.md), [035](../07-manifesto/035-route-b.md), [059e](../10-usa/059e-underdog-campaign.md) | no private referendum on the rule has yet been held; an underdog with such a number is a forecast |
| early elections stop being a trick of the government | the trick rests on a difference in speed: the government mobilises its quiet ones and public-sector employees with money within a week, the opposition rocks the apathetic for months (Serbia: 46 days); under the protocol the apathetic leave in the first days of the window, those who need no long persuading stay, and a public-sector employee can secretly take the payment — a short deadline gives nobody an advantage | found 28 Oct 2026; the architect's move ("the protocol minimises this trick: the apathetic leave, and those who stay are the ones who need no long persuading"), not planned | [057h §2.1](../09-other-countries/057h-serbia-2026.md), [048m art. 6](../08-implementation/048m-charter.md) | the share of the apathetic choosing in the first three days — a pilot measurement |

| there is no norm "to vote is a duty"; there is a practice of bringing-in, and the protocol buys it out | turnout is bought (Serbia: €600 m and 58.8 %), without bringing-in it is 43–44 % (Ireland); turnout = the core by payroll and habit + the herded + people with a stake, duty remains in questionnaires as the approved answer; the protocol pays the herded more and personally — the practice goes in the first cycle; duty is recorded for the first time: those who refused the money | found 28 Oct 2026; the architect's move ("long not a norm, judging by turnouts… most are herded in and certainly not by duty"), not planned | [040bk §2](../06-critique-arsenal/040bk-north.md), [040ba §1](../06-critique-arsenal/040ba-turnout-theory.md), [036e §4](../06-critique-arsenal/036e-nobel-fifth-circle.md) | the share of the core by habit and its behaviour in the first cycle — a pilot measurement |
| elections arranged as a commons by Ostrom's eight principles — better than the present system on all eight | the boundaries are set by the choice itself (three states, the sum balances); a local median and a local p; the rule is changed only by referendum; monitoring by the users (the counter, the parallel count, the one who chose nothing as monitor); graduated sanctions (the ladder of 048k §4b); a court within days on open data; the right to organise (route B); nesting courtyard → city → country; citizenship is not crowded out, because the rule is adopted by the community itself and the price stands on the exit, not on the act | found 28 Oct 2026; the Ostrom analysis on the architect's question, not planned | [040bl](../06-critique-arsenal/040bl-ostrom.md), [048k §4b](../08-implementation/048k-charter-inventory.md), [040as §3](../06-critique-arsenal/040as-walzer-sandel.md) | principles 4–6 exist on paper until the pilot (rules-in-use) — a measurement of 048l §4 |
| the referendum on the protocol takes place behind the veil of uncertainty, and the payment satisfies the generality principle | nobody at the referendum knows whether he will be a taker or a stayer next cycle (states, not types), so the rule is adopted without knowing one's gain — Buchanan's condition of justice; D is the same for every holder of the right — his principle of generality, while a targeted package to pensioners (Serbia 2026) is his counter-example; D is the one budget line the elected can neither repeal nor redirect (art. 14) | found 28 Oct 2026; the Buchanan analysis on the architect's question, not planned | [040bm](../06-critique-arsenal/040bm-buchanan.md), [013 §13.3](../03-theory/013-game-theory.md), [057h §2.6](../09-other-countries/057h-serbia-2026.md) | "who pays": the cost is explicit (1e: 3–4.5 % of the fund at half taking), not zero; one who opposes the rule and takes no money is an external cost, reduced, not removed |
| the sensor of dispersed knowledge is not disconnected but priced; the charter is nomos, not thesis | the objection "having bought the farmer's silence, the hall governs in a vacuum" (040b §4) is removed in Hayek's own terms: the ballot never carried his knowledge (one bit without intensity), the knowledge works in the prices of his market, and in the hall a sensor appears that was not there — when the pain exceeds D the farmer stays and the share of takers in his district falls; the sensor is silent while the signal is weaker than the price and switches itself on (states, not types). The charter is an abstract general rule, the same for all and not changeable by the elected (art. 14), against targeted packages and shifted dates; Hayek's demarchy (a hall by age) is the same aim by types, the protocol by states | found 28 Oct 2026; the Hayek analysis on the architect's question, not planned | [040bn](../06-critique-arsenal/040bn-hayek.md), [036b §6](../06-critique-arsenal/036b-nobel-second-circle.md), [040b §5](../06-critique-arsenal/040b-hanson-futarchy.md) | the farmer's "switching on" under real pain is reasoning, not a measurement (048l §4); the share of takers is the price of one good, not a vector of prices across questions |
| a hall of those who counted against a hall of those who did not | the blow "the stayers are no better, merely more stubborn and more vain" is accepted in full and turned: everyone in the hall compared D with the worth of the vote to himself, the taker counted too, only the one brought in did not count — and he is gone; a voter's stubbornness and self-assurance are readiness to act on one's conviction and calculation, which every thinker demanded of the citizen without an instrument to separate it; the fork — either the stayers are more stubborn and the hall consists of those everyone wanted, or not and the hall is no worse than today's. Alongside: "unfamiliar" ≠ "wrong"; man is inconstant — the rule asks every cycle; "on loan, not as a gift"; the prince's liberality with others' money — the targeted package | found 29 Oct 2026; the architect's move on Montaigne's blow | [040bo §3](../06-critique-arsenal/040bo-montaigne.md), [1g](001g-objections-index.md), [040b §5](../06-critique-arsenal/040b-hanson-futarchy.md) | readiness to act is attributed to the stayers logically; the share of the "showy" — a measurement of 048l §4 |
| passionarity gets an instrument, a unit and a refresh rate for the first time | refusing D is a drive that exceeded personal gain by a measured amount: an operational definition of Gumilev's quantity, described for forty years from chronicles after the fact; the unit is a share of the median, the frequency the cycle, the curve by p at referendums; the same instrument solves Dahl's "intensity problem" (1956); the dispute "trait or state" is settled by experiment on the stability of one person's choice from cycle to cycle; the instrument is coarse at the income edges and accurate on the middle class — more accurate than today's zero; the measurement is honest only because the refusal is voluntary | found 29 Oct 2026; the Gumilev analysis on the architect's question and his three moves | [040bp](../06-critique-arsenal/040bp-gumilev.md), [1h](001h-glossary.md), [048l §4](../08-implementation/048l-courtyard-pilot.md) | Gumilev's theory is not accepted; whether to call the quantity passionarity is the scientists' dispute; no absolute measurement, only relative to one's own median |
| a government elected by a hall with a stake does not multiply the apparatus but counts it | today a new department is a hundred votes brought in by the payroll list, so a politician multiplies departments by calculation; with a private choice the brought-in man can take D and not come, the bloc stops being reliable, and a department stops buying votes; in the hall are those who counted their own and refused D — they count departments and costs first; the apparatus is hired, with no lawful means of resistance, and sabotage degrades services and itself spurs automation (the fork); it pays the mayor to cut the town hall's expenses to report to the hall | found 29 Oct 2026; five moves of the architect | [019c §6k](../04-electoral-dynamics/019c-reform-by-subtraction.md), [036d §1](../06-critique-arsenal/036d-nobel-fourth-circle.md), [040bo §3](../06-critique-arsenal/040bo-montaigne.md) | one cycle of delay for honest figures; the boundary is where the law requires a person; "they will count" is a consequence of the hall's composition, not a measurement |
